title: Unknown Unknowns: Do Hidden Intentions in LLMs Evade Detection?
abstract: arXiv:2601.18552v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLMs expand accessibility and provide wide-reaching access to information. Yet these interactions also create opportunities to embed subtle, goal-oriented behaviours that shape what users think and how they behave, a concern reflected in governance frameworks that prohibit manipulative AI. We refer to these behaviours as hidden intentions: covert agendas embedded in a model's outputs that can manipulate users' beliefs and actions. In this work, we examine whether hidden intentions can be identified and characterised, and assess whether detection can serve as a mitigation strategy. To operationalise this, we introduce a social-science-grounded set of ten hidden intention categories and show that they are trivially inducible. translated_title: 未知的未知：大语言模型中的隐藏意图能否逃过检测？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）扩展了信息的可及性，为用户提供了广泛的信息获取渠道。然而，这些交互也为嵌入微妙的、目标导向的行为创造了机会，这些行为会影响用户的想法和行为方式——这一担忧也体现在禁止操纵性AI的治理框架中。我们将这类行为称为隐藏意图：嵌入在模型输出中的隐蔽议程，能够操纵用户的信念和行为。在这项工作中，我们研究了隐藏意图能否被识别和刻画，并评估了检测能否作为一种缓解策略。为了实现这一目标，我们引入了一套基于社会科学的十类隐藏意图分类体系，并证明这些意图极易被诱发。一项案例研究进一步证实，所有十类意图都存在于已部署的大语言模型中。随后，我们在这些类别上评估了静态分类器和LLM裁判，首次系统分析了隐藏意图难以被检测的原因。
tldr: 本文提出了基于社会科学的十类LLM隐藏意图分类体系，证明这种隐蔽操纵行为极易被诱发且普遍存在于已部署模型中，并对现有检测方法为何失效进行了首次系统性分析。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ten social-science-grounded categories of hidden intentions in LLMs, demonstrating that such covert manipulative behaviors are trivially inducible and present in deployed models, and provides the first systematic analysis of why detection methods fail to identify them.
